study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Kim et al., Nature Mental Health, 2024
study_identification_part.si4_title: Mapping cerebellar anatomical heterogeneity in mental and neurological illnesses

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Map normative development and aging of the cerebellum across the lifespan using >54k MRI scans; build voxel-wise and lobular normative models and apply them to clinical groups to quantify individual-level deviations and their associations with cognition and symptoms.

rci1_dataset_name.answer: Multi-site aggregated dataset (ABIDE; ADHD200; AOMIC ID1000; Beijing Enhanced; Cam-CAN; CoRR; DLBS; DS000119; DS000202; DS000222; Fcon1000; HBN; HCP; MPI Lemon; NKI-Rockland; OASIS-3; PING; SALD; SLIM; UK Biobank; and 100+ other studies)(Total 132)
rci1_dataset_name.reason: The paper clearly states the dataset names used in the training population. The main paper (page 5, Methods section) states: 'The cohort of individuals without diagnoses was obtained from 132 scanning sites, including various studies such as ABIDE, ADHD200, AOMIC ID1000, Beijing Enhanced, CAMCAN, CoRR, DLBS, DS000119, DS000202, DS000222, Fcon1000, HBN, HCP, MPI Lemon, NKI-Rockland, OASIS-3, PING, SALD, SLIM, and UK Biobank.' Supplementary Table 1 provides comprehensive information on all studies used. As there are more than five datasets, the answer follows the guideline format listing representative ones.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: The cohort of individuals without diagnoses was obtained from 132 scanning sites, including various studies such as ABIDE, ADHD200, AOMIC ID1000, Beijing Enhanced, CAMCAN, CoRR, DLBS, DS000119, DS000202, DS000222, Fcon1000, HBN, HCP, MPI Lemon, NKI-Rockland, OASIS-3, PING, SALD, SLIM, and UK Biobank. Data used in the preparation of this article were obtained from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) database (adni.loni.usc.edu).
rci1_dataset_name.location: Main paper, page 5, lines 138-142; Supplementary Table 1

rci2_hc_n.reason: Table 1 in the main manuscript clearly shows the training set for normative modeling contained 27,117 participants. The paper uses a train/test split for individuals without diagnosis, and normative models are trained on the training portion. The test set (26,985) was used for model evaluation and comparison with clinical groups.
